messages.author: 63607eb869df4dda
messages.subject: freq_poly with frequencies
parts:
Hi all,

I am attempting to construct a frequency polygon with frequencies on
the y-axis, but cannot seem to discover how to do this. A very simple
example:


d<-rnorm(100)
qplot(d, geom="freqpoly")


Instead of counts plotted on the y-axis I want frequency.

Thanks in advance,

Jason

messages.author: 63607eb869df4dda
messages.subject: Re: freq_poly with frequencies
parts:
Hi Patrick,

Thanks for your reply.  Unfortunately, that does not do what I want.  Instead of a density plot I want frequencies (i.e. no. obs. in a bin/total no. obs).  I am working around by using ..count.. and simply relabeling the y-axis with frequencies instead of absolute counts.  Of course this doesn't work if you have multiple groups and they don't have the same number of total observations.

Thanks again, Jason

On Mon, Jul 11, 2011 at 6:35 PM, patrick kilduff <dpki...@yahoo.com> wrote:
hi jason -

does this do what you want?

qplot(d, ..density.., geom = "freqpoly")

- patrick

messages.author: 91481440fd4fef18
messages.subject: Re: freq_poly with frequencies
parts:
There's also the option of using y=..ncount.. which normalizes each group by its maximum number of observation (i.e., scales all groups to a maximum of 1). It's not the same as normalizing by the total number of events, of course (which is more like making it a probability).
You can make the bincount yourself outside of ggplot, though, and simply normalize afterwards.

Moritz
